blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-08-08. The official AdministrableFA2 implementation permits any token administrator to call burn(owner, token_id, token_amount) against the named owner's balance rather than only the administrator's own balance. Live token_id 0 administrator entries include Youves engine contracts, and recent applied burn operations show an engine caller differing from the holder whose uUSD was burned. This is a current allowance-free arbitrary-holder burn primitive, so uUSD resolves direct Yes. Material USDt collateral supplies additional upstream Tether freeze exposure.

oracleRisk.summary: Youves uUSD has six active V3 engines and three legacy but debt-bearing engines. Eight branches accept millisecond Ubinetic report timestamps in a seconds-based nominal 900-second check, making freshness effectively unbounded; the legacy SIRS branch was fail-closed because its required BTC/USD epoch was 301 epochs stale. Liquidation is branch-local and permissionless, with no funded deficit backstop.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 ORCL curation
branchApplicability.rationale: The official registry and SDK enumerate collateral-specific uUSD engines with distinct oracle contracts and liquidation ratios. Finalized Tezos state shows all three registry-labelled legacy engines still carry positive debt, so active and legacy debt-bearing engines require separate branches.

branches.label: uUSD / XTZ V1 legacy debt
branches.summary: The legacy XTZ V1 engine remains debt-bearing and reads a single composite XTZ/USD path whose nominal 900-second check cannot reject millisecond report timestamps.

feeds.path: Ubinetic USDT/USD and XTZ/USDT reports -> Youves XTZ/USD composite -> V1 vault health and liquidation

branches.fallbackBehavior: The engine has one configured target-price oracle and no automatic secondary. Every composite component must return or the transaction fails closed, but millisecond report timestamps are compared with Tezos seconds and therefore make the nominal 900-second freshness check effectively unbounded.

collateralParameters.note: Official legacy collateral documentation and the pinned SDK record a 300% target ratio and 200% emergency/liquidation ratio. Finalized engine debt was 2,277.641100920260 uUSD.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Any caller may burn uUSD against a vault below the 200% emergency ratio and receive XTZ at the legacy liquidation payout; execution is atomic.
branches.backstop: No funded liquidation backstop is active. The legacy bailout/minter-conversion feature was a holder conversion right, not bad-debt insurance, and Youves now labels it inactive.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: No active shutdown or deficit-redistribution module is documented. Liquidation depends on a caller supplying uUSD; debt that cannot be economically liquidated remains with its vault rather than moving to a Stability Pool.

branches.fallbackBehavior: The finalized engine storage names one target-price oracle and no automatic secondary. collateralParameters.note: Legacy docs and SDK record a 300% target and 200% emergency ratio. Finalized engine debt was 77.881302640981 uUSD.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Any caller may burn uUSD against a vault below the 200% emergency ratio and receive tzBTC at the legacy liquidation payout; execution is atomic.
branches.backstop: No Stability Pool, insurance reserve, or debt auction is connected to this engine; the legacy tzBTC branch is excluded from the now-inactive bailout conversion feature.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: No active shutdown or deficit redistribution is documented. Liquidation requires caller-supplied uUSD, and unrecovered debt remains vault-local rather than being socialized.

branches.label: uUSD / SIRS V2 legacy debt
branches.summary: The legacy SIRS V2 engine remains debt-bearing, but its required generic BTC/USD component was 301 epochs stale and made price-dependent engine actions fail closed at the fixed level.

feeds.path: SIRS/tzBTC LP oracle KT1GqQ... plus generic BTC/USD oracle KT1Kzd... -> callback-composed SIRS/USD scratch value at KT1VCF... -> V2 vault health and liquidation

branches.fallbackBehavior: The engine has one custom target-price oracle and no alternate route; the LP callback value is transaction scratch, not a durable cached fallback. At the fixed level, generic BTC/USD last_epoch 1981969 was 301 epochs behind current epoch 1982270 and exceeded the four-epoch window, so PRICE_TOO_OLD made price-dependent mint, withdrawal, and liquidation actions unavailable.

collateralParameters.note: Legacy docs and SDK record a 300% target and 200% emergency ratio. Finalized engine debt was 9,235.129323262868 uUSD.

branches.liquidationMechanism: The branch is designed for permissionless atomic liquidation below the 200% emergency ratio, but liquidation was unavailable at level 14059094 because the mandatory BTC/USD leg reverted PRICE_TOO_OLD after 301 stale epochs.
branches.backstop: No Stability Pool, insurance reserve, or debt auction is connected to this engine; Youves explicitly excludes SIRS from the obsolete bailout conversion feature.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: No active shutdown or deficit redistribution is documented. Liquidation requires caller-supplied uUSD, and unrecovered debt remains vault-local rather than being socialized.

branches.label: uUSD / USDt V3
branches.summary: The active USDt V3 engine uses one threshold-signed Ubinetic path whose nominal 900-second check cannot reject millisecond report timestamps.

feeds.path: Ubinetic USDT/USD report at KT1Exb... -> composite inverse at KT1USE... -> V3 vault health and liquidation

branches.fallbackBehavior: The composite has no alternate feed and all required calls must return or INVALID_VIEW fails closed. Its nominal 900-second check compares millisecond report timestamps with Tezos seconds, making freshness effectively unbounded rather than contract-enforced.

collateralParameters.note: Finalized storage records collateral_ratio 110%, which base_tracker_engine_v3 enforces on mint and withdrawal and implies 90.909091% maximum LTV; settlement_ratio is the 115% holder-conversion term, not a liquidation threshold. Debt was 11,172,864.355705194083 uUSD.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Permissionless atomic liquidation burns caller-supplied uUSD and transfers USDt; payout is capped by the lower of the vault ratio and the configured 110% payout.
branches.backstop: No funded liquidation backstop is connected to V3. Youves states V3 savings pools no longer support the bailout/minter-conversion feature.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: There is no active Stability Mechanism or shutdown redistribution. An insolvent vault can be liquidated at its actual collateral ratio only when a caller supplies uUSD; otherwise debt remains vault-local.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: UUSD is tracked as a single-chain or natively issued asset for this review, with no source-verified cross-chain route that creates durable supply. Bridge-route scoring is therefore informational and does not add a third-party route penalty.
bridgeRouteRisk.sourceFreeRationale: The tracked UUSD contract is on Tezos and reviewed Youves docs describe local synthetic-asset contracts rather than a cross-chain route.
